questions.q: In pattern drafting, what is the function of the 'brown paper' (or pattern paper)?
options: It is worn by the client to test the fit.
It serves as the base material on which the exact body shapes and measurements are drawn.
It is dissolved in water to make liquid starch.
It is ironed permanently onto the fabric to make it stiff.
questions.explain: Pattern or brown paper is used as a template to draft out the calculated body measurements before transferring those shapes onto actual fabric for cutting.

questions.q: When taking a woman's body measurements for a blouse, how should the measuring tape be placed to determine the 'bust measurement'?
options: Around the narrowest part of the abdomen.
From the nape of the neck down to the waist.
Horizontally around the back and across the fullest part of the chest (bust apex).
Vertically from the shoulder to the knee.
questions.explain: To get an accurate bust measurement, the tape measure must be wrapped entirely around the body, passing over the shoulder blades at the back and the fullest, most prominent part of the breasts.

questions.q: What does the term 'seam allowance' refer to when drafting basic bodice and skirt patterns?
options: The discount given by the tailor on the price of the dress.
The extra fabric added beyond the actual stitching line to ensure the pieces can be joined securely without unraveling.
A decorative pocket placed on the chest.
The total amount of thread allowed for one sewing session.
questions.explain: A seam allowance is a crucial margin of extra fabric (usually between 1.5 cm and 2 cm) added around the drafted pattern line, giving the tailor room to sew the seam without making the dress too tight.

questions.q: In fashion designing, after using instructions to sketch a style on paper, the drawn 'style lines' help the tailor identify:
options: The price of the fabric.
The position of darts, seams, pleats, and necklines.
The customer's exact age.
The brand of sewing machine used.
questions.explain: Style lines in a fashion sketch visually communicate the construction details and design features (like where the waist sits, dart placements, and collar shape) to the person drafting the pattern.

questions.q: Tailor's chalk is an essential tool in fashion designing. What is its specific use?
options: To permanently dye the fabric a different color.
To draw non-permanent markings, lines, and patterns directly onto the fabric.
To glue two pieces of fabric securely together.
To wash off tough grease stains from a dress.
questions.explain: Tailor's chalk is used to make temporary guide marks on fabric indicating where to cut, sew, or place darts. The chalk marks easily brush or wash off without ruining the garment.
